question: Can entropy of the single next token after an artificially appended stop-thinking marker provide a cheap, model-agnostic signal for halting reasoning once additional chain-of-thought no longer improves answer probability?

key_findings.claim: EAT is a one-token predictive-entropy probe, not entropy of the reasoning tokens or a direct correctness estimate.
key_findings.evidence: At checkpoints in an unfinished reasoning trace, the method appends </think> plus an optional final-answer prefix and measures entropy over the next-token distribution. The reasoning-dependent term equals the negative component of a proposed information-gain expression, while correctness is evaluated separately with many answer rollouts.

key_findings.claim: The stopping rule detects stabilization rather than low entropy.
key_findings.evidence: An exponential moving mean and variance are updated at each reasoning block; generation stops when debiased variance falls below a global threshold or the model emits </think>. Thus a stable high or misleading proxy trajectory can also trigger exit, while an unsolvable unstable trajectory consumes the full cap.

key_findings.claim: Across the selected math and science settings, threshold sweeps yield a better accuracy-token frontier than assigning one fixed token budget to every item.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments with DeepSeek-R1 Qwen-8B/Llama-70B, Qwen3-4B, and Claude 3.7 report 12-22% token reduction on MATH500 and AIME2025 without loss at selected operating points. The improvement comes from using fewer tokens on traces whose EAT variance stabilizes early.

key_findings.claim: Small proxy models can monitor larger or API-only reasoners in the demonstrated cases, but cross-model calibration is empirical and narrow.
key_findings.evidence: A 1.5B model is used to halt a 70B Llama reasoner and a local Qwen3-4B probe monitors eight Claude 3.7 AIME questions. Proxy computation can overlap API streaming, but no broad matrix of proxy/target families, adversarial disagreements, or distribution shifts is reported.

key_findings.claim: The headline GPQA curve is conditioned on solvability and therefore does not measure end-to-end behavior over the original task distribution.
key_findings.evidence: The main GPQA plots retain only questions whose eventual Pass@1 exceeds 0.8. On unfiltered or unsolvable questions EAT often never stabilizes and spends the entire token budget; some questions also exhibit decreasing Pass@1.

method.core_idea: Periodically force an answer boundary in the current reasoning prefix, measure next-token entropy, and stop once the recent entropy trajectory becomes stable.
method.mechanism: After each newline-delimited block, the target or a proxy model scores the same question and accumulated reasoning followed by </think> and usually 'Final answer:'. Vocabulary entropy of the next token becomes EAT. An EMA with alpha near 0.2 tracks mean and variance; a threshold delta controls the accuracy-compute frontier. Evaluation estimates checkpoint correctness with K sampled final-answer rollouts, but those rollouts are not used by the deployed stopping rule.
assumptions: Entropy of the first answer token correlates with correctness saturation across tasks and output formats.
Appending the boundary/prefix elicits the same answer distribution the model would produce after naturally finishing reasoning.
A fixed variance threshold and EMA timescale transfer across item difficulty and model families.
A smaller proxy's uncertainty dynamics faithfully track the larger target model's remaining reasoning value.

techniques.role: Queries the answer distribution at intermediate reasoning prefixes without generating a full answer.
Uses full-vocabulary entropy of one post-boundary token as the monitoring statistic.
Halts when the recent EAT trajectory is sufficiently stable.
Computes the stopping signal with a smaller local model when target logits are unavailable.
Sweeps thresholds and compares aggregate Pass@1 against total generated tokens.

evaluations.setting: MATH500 and AIME2025 with DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, and Qwen3-4B reasoning models.
evaluations.metric: Aggregate rollout-estimated Pass@1 versus reasoning-token usage.
evaluations.result: Selected EAT thresholds reduce tokens by roughly 12-22% while preserving reported accuracy, with adaptive budgets improving the frontier.
evaluations.baseline: A uniform per-question token cap and number-of-unique-answers stopping with K rollouts.

evaluations.setting: Black-box monitoring of Llama-70B with a 1.5B proxy and Claude 3.7 on the first eight AIME2025 questions with Qwen3-4B.
evaluations.metric: Stopping position, correctness, token/time savings, and probe latency.
evaluations.result: The proxy variants retain useful EAT trajectories; Claude examples save at least about one minute and local probe time fits under streaming latency.
evaluations.baseline: Using target-model logits where available and waiting for natural/full-budget completion.

evaluations.setting: MATH500 comparison against five-token confidence and rollout-based answer convergence.
evaluations.result: EAT is reported to match the short-rollout confidence frontier at about one-fifth probe cost; #UA@K requires K at least 16 for a reliable signal and rollouts dominate cost.

limitations: Main GPQA results filter to eventually solvable questions, overstating whole-distribution efficiency.
Pass@1 trajectories used as ground truth require up to 128 stochastic rollouts per checkpoint and remain sampling estimates.
Theoretical information-gain language does not prove that one-token entropy is calibrated to correctness or marginal value of reasoning.
The final-answer prefix materially affects some models, making the signal prompt- and tokenizer-dependent.
Long-form answer domains such as code can have an uninformative first answer token.
The Claude study uses only eight AIME items, and tool-calling results suggest reasoning was unnecessary in that setting.
failure_modes: A confidently wrong answer can yield low, stable entropy and stop too early.
An unsolvable or indecisive problem can keep variance high and consume the entire cap.
A proxy model can settle on a different answer or reasoning phase than the target model.
Repeated generic first tokens after the answer prefix can stabilize while later answer content remains uncertain.
EMA initialization, block boundaries, or oscillating conclusions can move the threshold crossing substantially.
reusable_insights: Evaluate adaptive computation with an accuracy-cost frontier, not a single hand-picked threshold.
Account for monitoring overhead and permit it to overlap target decoding where possible.
Separate progress signals for solvable cases from give-up signals for persistently unsolved cases.
Test proxy monitors as a full target-by-proxy matrix rather than one favorable pair.
Use counterfactual answer probes to measure marginal reasoning value without expensive full rollouts.
open_questions: Can a calibrated risk-control rule turn EAT into a finite-sample guarantee on accuracy degradation?
What complementary statistic should terminate confidently unsolved traces before the maximum budget?
Does entropy over a structured multi-token answer prefix outperform one-token EAT at comparable cost?
How stable are thresholds across languages, tokenizers, code generation, agents, and distribution shift?
Can proxy-target disagreement itself be used as an abstention or continue-reasoning signal?

competitive_landscape.title: Answer Convergence as a Signal for Early Stopping in Reasoning
competitive_landscape.difference: Answer-convergence stopping samples complete answers at intermediate prefixes and watches agreement. EAT targets the same saturation point with a one-token entropy probe, greatly reducing overhead but relying on access to logits or a calibrated proxy.

competitive_landscape.title: Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. establish overthinking and study interventions for excessive reasoning. EAT contributes an online entropy-trajectory detector and adaptive stopping evaluation rather than primarily diagnosing the inefficiency.

competitive_landscape.title: Early Stopping Chain-of-Thoughts in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This concurrent work also targets early termination of chain-of-thought. EAT's distinctive mechanism is the entropy immediately after a forced stop marker and its variance, including small-proxy monitoring of black-box reasoners.

competitive_landscape.title: Conformal Thinking: Risk Control for Reasoning on a Compute Budget
competitive_landscape.difference: Conformal Thinking adds explicit risk control to adaptive reasoning under a compute budget. It addresses the guarantee gap left by EAT, while EAT supplies a particularly cheap unsupervised trajectory statistic and black-box proxy construction.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim EAT is a simple, inexpensive, adaptive early-exit signal whose stabilization tracks Pass@1 saturation and can be computed by small proxies for black-box reasoning models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Equations 5-8 and Algorithm 1 define the probe; Figures 3-6 and appendices compare threshold frontiers, proxy settings, and failure cases.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The one-token post-</think> entropy trajectory and cross-model proxy deployment are concrete additions to a crowded overthinking/answer-convergence literature. The work does not establish calibration, risk guarantees, or whole-distribution gains on GPQA, and its strongest novelty is low monitoring cost rather than a general solution to deciding when reasoning is complete.

reviewer_notes: Read all 27 pages of the pinned PDF, including algorithm details, efficiency accounting, full GPQA error analysis, Claude/proxy traces, ablations, prompts, and long qualitative examples. Primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23 across overthinking diagnosis, answer convergence, concurrent early stopping, and subsequent risk-controlled stopping. Main-text filtered results are explicitly distinguished from unfiltered failure behavior.
